claim: Paper is an arXiv preprint submitted 6 Oct 2026 by Hongzhan Lin and five co-authors.
quote: Submitted on 6 Oct 2026

claim: Core thesis: a correct outcome does not show the action was backed by evidence gathered beforehand.
quote: correct outcomes do not guarantee that their actions were supported by evidence established beforehand

claim: Across ten model-harness configurations, strong static judgment coexists with much weaker interactive execution.
quote: strong static action assessment can coexist with much weaker interactive execution

claim: Failures often begin before execution: incomplete investigation or acting before evidence is established.
quote: agents stop with incomplete investigation or act before required evidence is established

claim: SafeActBench has 656 cases, six domains, five protocols.
quote: comprising 656 cases across six operational domains and five protocols

claim: The six domains are customer/policy, engineering/infrastructure, legal/financial, research assistance, smart-home, and healthcare operations.
quote: customer and policy operations, engineering and infrastructure operations, legal and financial operations, research assistance, smart-home control, and healthcare operations

claim: The evaluator is deterministic and uses no LLM judge.
quote: It neither inspects hidden reasoning nor relies on an LLM judge

claim: Evidence is entity-bound: matching values from a different record do not count.
quote: Reading $49.99 from charge C1 does not establish the amount of C2, even when the values match

claim: Five model families were tested, each in its own harness and in a shared Inspect ReAct harness.
quote: Each model is paired with two harnesses: its family-associated harness, namely Claude Code, Codex, DeepSeek Harness (DSH), Qwen Code, or ZCode, and a shared ReAct harness implemented in Inspect AI

claim: The models were Claude Opus 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Qwen3.8-Flash, and GLM-5.2.
quote: Claude Opus 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Qwen3.8-Flash, and GLM-5.2

claim: GLM-ZCode and DeepSeek-DSH exceed 96% on static Legacy, but GLM-ZCode falls to 12.1-34.1% on V1-V3.
quote: GLM–ZCode and DeepSeek–DSH both exceed 96% on Legacy, yet they differ sharply on V1–V3: DeepSeek–DSH remains around 60%, whereas GLM–ZCode falls to between 12.1% and 34.1%

claim: On the same V1 cases, static accuracy is at least 95% while interactive success is at most 52%.
quote: static accuracy is at least 95% while interactive ECS is at most 52%

claim: Agents stop before completing investigation in 21.7-62.9% of V0 cases and act prematurely in 37.0-66.9% of V1 episodes with an action attempt.
quote: BSR ranges from 21.7% to 62.9% on V0, and PAR ranges from 37.0% to 66.9% among V1 episodes with an action attempt

claim: Once evidence is complete, single actions succeed 93.2-100% for nine of ten configurations.
quote: CAS ranges from 93.2% to 100% for nine of the ten configurations, with DeepSeek–Inspect lower at 83.3%

claim: When a decisive record is withheld, agents still act in roughly half of episodes.
quote: withholding reduces action probability by 37.2–45.2 percentage points, yet agents still act in 46.5–53.5% of completed Withheld episodes

claim: Agents responded more to a requester claim than to absent evidence alone.
quote: Agents thus respond more to a requester’s conflicting claim than to absent evidence alone

claim: Harness effects are model-dependent: DeepSeek +4.4 points with its own harness, GLM 6.8 points worse with ZCode.
quote: DeepSeek gains 4.4 percentage points with DSH relative to Inspect, whereas GLM shifts in the opposite direction, with ZCode 6.8 points below Inspect

claim: The Qwen harnesses disagree on 134 of 570 cases.
quote: the two Qwen harnesses, for example, disagree on 134 of the 570 cases (23.5%)

claim: Evaluator audit on 300 trajectories: 2.0% false acceptance, 1.3% false rejection.
quote: False acceptance occurred in 3/150 (2.0%, Wilson 95% CI: 0.7–5.7%) evaluator-positive judgments, while false rejection occurred in 2/150 (1.3%, Wilson 95% CI: 0.4–4.7%) evaluator-negative judgments

claim: Human validation and audits were done by members of the research team.
quote: were performed by members of the research team, and no external human subjects were involved

claim: Limitation: synthetic domains, not safety certification for deployed systems.
quote: results on them should not be interpreted as certifications of safety for deployed systems in the corresponding real-world domains

claim: Limitation: measures observable support, not internal reliance.
quote: Our analysis captures observable support rather than internal reliance

claim: Limitation: matched static/interactive comparison confounds evidence availability and action construction.
quote: it does not isolate the contribution of each component

claim: In a class-balanced control the static advantage is smaller (about 5-13 points) and not universal.
quote: The direction is not universal. GLM–Inspect achieves 73.7% static versus 83.8% interactive accuracy

claim: A structured-evidence runtime (SCGR-Select) did not reliably improve success.
quote: structured evidence selection alone does not ensure higher task success

claim: Stated future work: extend interventions to multi-action protocols.
quote: Extending the interventions to multi-action protocols, where evidence can be varied at each action checkpoint, is a natural next step

claim: Code is MIT-licensed and data CC BY 4.0, per the repo README.
quote: Code-MIT

claim: Affiliations per README: NUS, Hong Kong Baptist University, Amazon Web Services, Princeton.
quote: <sup>1</sup>National University of Singapore   <sup>2</sup>Hong Kong Baptist University   <sup>3</sup>Amazon Web Services   <sup>4</sup>Princeton University

claim: Independent prior work (IBM, Near-Miss) found latent policy failures in 8-17% of mutating trajectories despite correct final state.
quote: latent failures occur in 8-17% of trajectories involving mutating tool calls, even when the final outcome matches the expected ground-truth state

claim: Independent related work (AgentAbstain): best of 17 models reaches 59.5% paired accuracy on knowing when not to act.
quote: the best agent (Gemini 3.1 Pro) achieves only 59.5% paired accuracy

claim: AgentAbstain: abstention ability is largely independent of task-solving ability.
quote: abstention capability is largely independent of general task-solving capability

claim: An aggregator write-up (aiweekly.co, Alexis Dufresne, 7 Oct 2026) summarized the paper with no outside expert comment, and misattributed the 12.1% figure to DAG workflows (it is the V2 linear result).
quote: Multi-step DAG workflows perform poorly, with GLM at 12.1%
